purpose: Full-corpus classification audit of every molecule newly fail-closed by has_unresolved_specified_tetrahedral_stereo (crates/chematic-inchi/src/native/convert.rs), beyond the originally disclosed 4663/4664 pair.
corpus: ~/Downloads/SMILES.csv, 5000 molecules, the project's standard reference corpus
rdkit_oracle_version: 2026.03.3 (isolated venv, independent of chematic Python bindings)

acceptance_criteria_update.framing: Detected via full-corpus structural audit, not a narrower estimate that undercounted scope.

audit_scope: All 12 molecules newly flagged verification_unavailable under StandardInchiString/StandardInchiKey/IsotopeIgnored (excludes the 1 pre-existing native-InChI kekulization failure at corpus idx=2149, which is unrelated to this guard, and separately includes the 2 already-disclosed 4663/4664 fixture molecules as a reference anchor, not part of the 12 audited).
method: Per specified-chiral atom: chematic legacy CIP (assign_cip), chematic accurate CIP (assign_cip_with_mode, CipMode::Accurate), tetrahedral_stereo_neighbors resolution, cross-checked against an independent RDKit 2026.03.3 oracle (Chem.FindMolChiralCenters(includeUnassigned=True, useLegacyImplementation=False), rdCIPLabeler.AssignCIPLabels, Chem.MolToInchi /t layer). Renumbering stability checked both sides (8 random atom-order respellings via chematic random_smiles / RDKit RenumberAtoms).

classification_scheme.A: genuinely stereogenic, legacy CIP unresolved, accurate CIP resolves
classification_scheme.B: genuinely stereogenic, both chematic CIP modes unresolved
classification_scheme.C: specified tag on non-stereogenic or constitutionally equivalent center

atom_level_tally_over_12_new_molecules.note: legacy_resolved_baseline atoms are the already-correctly-ranked stereocenters within these same 12 molecules (not part of the +14 newly fail-closed count); included in the audit rows for completeness.

molecule_level_summary.example_case_A: corpus idx=1567 (NS(=O)(=O)OC[C@@]12CCCC[C@@H]1CCC2): legacy fails on the ring-fusion atom, accurate + RDKit both resolve it to plain 'R'.
molecule_level_summary.example_case_B: corpus idx=443 and idx=590 (tricyclic-cage bridgehead atoms 29 and 18 respectively): chematic's accurate engine reports Tied, RDKit's own rdCIPLabeler leaves the same atom unlabeled ('Tet_CCW' -- defined parity, no CIP descriptor). Both independent, state-of-the-art CIP engines agree no label exists; not a chematic-specific defect.

false_positive_rate: 0/12 molecules (0/28 audited atoms) -- every atom the guard flags corresponds to a real RDKit-confirmed (or RDKit-agreeing-unresolvable) stereocenter; none are constitutionally non-stereogenic.
false_negative_note: Not separately re-derived here since deduplicate_verified already runs identity_verify unconditionally over all 5000 corpus molecules (not just these 12) -- the full corpus n_verification_unavailable=15 total already reflects every molecule the guard fires on; no additional un-flagged offender exists in this corpus by construction of that full run.
unrelated_defect_noted_not_fixed_here: 8 of the 12 molecules (196, 1567, 1609, 4047, 4178, 4412, 4509, 4745) also intersect the project's pre-existing, already-tracked canonical-SMILES relabeling-residual defect class (random-respelling round-trip instability). This is a separate, out-of-scope bug -- ring/cage-heavy stereocenters simply happen to be the same population that stresses both issues. Not modified by this PR.
conclusion: All 12 molecules classify as A or B (mixed for 2 of them). Zero C, zero D, zero E. verification_unavailable=15 is adopted as the correct, fully-audited value -- not an estimate.
